title: Nornyx agentic runtime adapter-conformance report
description: Observed runtime behavior of an installed nornyx-agentic-adapters build against the exact framework versions named in the report. Cooperative Tier 2, declared wrapped surfaces only. Distinct from the static nornyx.adapter_conformance.v0.7 contract report, which validates declared shape with execution disabled.

safety.description: What this conformance run actually did. Distinct from the core evidence validator's safety block, which describes a process that executes nothing: this kit really does invoke governed actions and drive framework executors.

guarded_suites.description: Which suites actually ran under the outbound guard. Named rather than a bare boolean so a reader can tell exactly what was covered.

blocked_outbound_attempts.description: Observed count of outbound calls the guard blocked. A blocked attempt means the network was not reached; this is deliberately not restated as a 'network was used' flag, which would invert its meaning.

models_called.description: No external model is called. The framework suites drive a scripted, offline, in-process LLM to keep a native run deterministic; nothing leaves the process.

external_connectors_used.description: Structural property of the kit's design, not a measurement: it executes no connector.

credentials_loaded.description: Structural property of the kit's design, not a measurement: it loads no credentials.

declared_status.description: Read from the adapter's exported CoverageInventory. 'not_declared' is used only for boundaries that are not framework surfaces at all.

outcome.description: 'not_representable' means the case cannot exist on this surface at all. It is not a skip and not a pass, and it must name a covered_by case that does prove the behavior.

execution_path.description: 'native' means the framework's own executor drove the call and is the only path that can substantiate a native claim; 'direct' calls the adapter wrapper without the executor.

event_order.description: 'recorded' preserves the exact commit order, which any ordering claim requires. 'normalized' is sorted-unique and permitted only where a framework executor, not the adapter, controls repetition.

decision_events.description: Decision-event types in the order the adapter's own recorder committed them, unless event_order is 'normalized'. Repeats are meaningful and preserved.

observation_events.description: Observation event types in the order the adapter's own recorder committed them, unless event_order is 'normalized'. Repeats are meaningful and preserved.

decision_precedes_observation.description: Whether every recorded observation followed at least one recorded decision event. Absent when the case recorded no observation, rather than vacuously true.

evidence_validation.description: Schema validity and binding consistency of the recorded stream. Never a claim that the events are true.

evidence_diagnostics.description: Sorted unique diagnostic codes the evidence validator reported. A case documenting a known non-validating path asserts which failure it observed, so an unrelated regression cannot hide behind the same bare 'fail'.

count_check.description: A counted observation and the assertion actually made about it. 'at_least' omits the observed value because a framework executor, not the adapter, controls repetition on that path.

occurrence_summary.description: Determinism-safe facts derived from an occurrence-aware stream. Raw occurrence ids are deliberately absent: LangGraph mints a fresh task id per process. 'collided' detects one specific shape: two different logical operations recorded under one occurrence id.
